title: Completeness of the 3-SAT to clique reduction
statement: Let $V$ be any type and let $f$ be a list of $m$ clauses, each consisting of three literals over $V$. If some truth assignment satisfies every clause of $f$, then the conflict graph has a clique of size $m$. Its vertices are clause-position pairs, and two are adjacent exactly when they come from different clauses and their literals are not opposite occurrences of the same variable.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a finite list of three-literal clauses over $V$
replaced:
Let $f$ be a 3-CNF formula consisting of $m$ clauses, and let its conflict graph be the
simple graph on the vertices $\langle c, \ell\rangle$ (clause index $c$, literal
position $\ell$) in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when they belong to
different clauses and their literals do not conflict. If $f$ is satisfiable, then this
conflict graph has an $m$-clique.
